note: The 1st, 4th and 5th chords as triads moved from the top three strings to the D, G and B strings: new shapes for chords the learner knows. The key and tempo move (any key, 60 to 80 bpm), the chords are chord tokens counted the long way once, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same in another key.

exercise.title: Triads, one string set lower
exercise.why: Every three neighbouring strings hold the same triads in new shapes, so moving a drill one string set over makes a new drill from chords you know.

cells.text:
The tab below holds three chords of {{=key}}. {{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track, and follow the tab. Each chord is a triad on the D, G and B strings: strike the three strings together on every beat.
Practice until each new shape lands on beat 1.
{{?key}}In another key the shapes sit on other frets, and each chord keeps its shape on the D, G and B strings.
